title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
Criminals used AI-generated video and audio to impersonate a real immigration attorney on social media, creating hundreds of fake profiles across TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram. The fraudulent content promised immigration services in exchange for cash payments. The scam targeted vulnerable immigrants seeking legal help, some of whom lost thousands of dollars before discovering the deception.

This is a case of impersonation enabled by generative AI, deployed at scale through social platforms without authentication. The criminals obtained the attorney's likeness and voice and used AI systems to create convincing but false video testimonials and contracts. The deployment lacked any verification mechanism that would have allowed potential clients to confirm they were contacting a real attorney, such as official account verification or requiring direct contact through verified legal channels.

It is not established how the criminals obtained the attorney's likeness and voice, or whether the social media platforms had systems in place that failed to catch the impersonation or were circumvented by the fraudsters.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of an elaborate artificial intelligence fraud scheme. Criminals have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos using his likeness to scam vulnerable immigrants. The fraudulent videos and testimonials promise services like US residency assistance and immigration detention release in exchange for cash payments ranging up to $2,200. Leal first discovered the problem when potential clients began calling his office after seeing the fake content online.

The scam has grown significantly over the past three months, prompting Leal to hire an anti-piracy company to combat the fraud. The company has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles across social media platforms, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. Fraudsters typically direct victims to contact them through WhatsApp, then send phony contracts and request payments via Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App. Leal is warning immigrants to verify anyone offering legal services online and plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the scheme's origins.
